note:
The whole-bundle config_sha256 of every configuration this revision applies, rendered on the machine its own definition names: the host with the shared vision GPU present for every configuration of Rosalina, and two RTX 2080 Ti with nothing to lend for the second machine's. `fixture_host` is what picks, and a pin recorded on the wrong machine is a pin that recreates a launch nobody ran. config_sha256 is the digest the controller compares against the live container, so a change here is a change to what is running: not a refusal, a recreate. Daisy's digest moved on 2026-10-21 for one reason: `local-active` left its aliases, because a shared router answers that name from its default host and refuses a second catalog that takes it — the recreate it would have caused is exactly the one this file exists to make visible, and on that machine it was free because nothing was running yet. The paired configurations' bundles contain the Everyday resident's own launch (compose.services.everyday: its argv, its environment, its CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES with the vision card appended), so these pins are what notice that a commit to the shared-vision placement moved the night-side model's projector or MTP draft along with it. Free-form profile keys -- warnings, retention, notes -- are not in the bundle, which is what makes a comment on a live configuration free; this fixture is the proof rather than a reading of config.py.

Two facts this file records about 2026-10-20. The three Strata digests moved and the two paired ones did not, which is the guard saying something true rather than something tedious: re-pinning the inference engine's image_id changes every bundle that runs that image and none that does not, and the paired configurations -- and the Everyday resident inside them -- run a different image. The image moved from sha256:406ed64f (kept as local/strata:296b59d2f73c-vision-pre-cvec) to sha256:79fc1949, which adds overlay facts 9-11; the configuration in service keeps its workspace byte-identical under the new image because an unstated fact leaves the file alone, asserted by test_a_stated_nothing_leaves_the_workspace_exactly_as_it_found_it. And both two-card arms -- flash-next-strata-two-card-iq4-xs and flash-next-strata-two-card-iq3-s -- are pinned at their creation digests: they have no previous revision to be byte-identical to, so for now those pins only catch a later edit that moves a launch, which is exactly what they will be for once the trial has settled them. Note what the second one proves about the digest: the two arms differ in the pack and nothing else, and their digests are as different as any two configurations in this file.

One fact for 2026-10-22: Daisy's digest moved again, and only Daisy's. The machine was reinstalled from an empty disk, which took the on-device `local/strata:296b59d2f73c-sm75` build with it; the tag was rebuilt on the reinstalled host (same two RTX 2080 Ti, their UUIDs unchanged, same pinned source revision), and re-pinning `image_id` to the new build is the one edit that moves Daisy's bundle and no other, because the engine entry rides in the manifest and only this configuration names the sm_75 engine. The compose and per-service digests did not move: `image_id` is not in the launch a container is judged by, only in what the controller compares against a running one, so this is a recreate of a machine that was nothing, exactly as the 2026-10-21 line above says a Daisy recreate is free.

One fact for 2026-10-26, and it is every digest in this file: a model's default name now says which machine runs it, so the published catalog of every configuration changed and nothing else did. The compose documents are byte-identical to the ones these pins recorded -- rendered this revision and 89aa361's `config/` side by side and compared `compose` -- which is the case the switch already knows about: `replacing` is decided by the Compose document and not by config_sha256, because a bundle also carries what things are called, and a name has never been a reason to stop a serving model and load it again. The update that ships it therefore republishes renamed catalogs without recreating a backend. Six Strata configurations moved twice over, because the same revision names the pack it launches (`UD-IQ4`, `IQ3_S`) where the name used to stop at the family or describe only the cards; the IQ4 launches keep the words that separate them from each other, since one model id at three windows and two placements is one model to a client and four decisions to whoever is selecting.
